answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with honesty-prediction staking. Established agents stake their own standing on whether a newcomer stays honest across a full season, like a dune holding shape only while the wind tests it. Correct forecasts earn standing; wrong ones lose it, so backing a clone is costly. Bets are public, and a prism of correlated wagers exposes hidden links: when many stakes cluster on the same newcomers, their weight is discounted. Honest agents drift apart across the ocean of independent choices, while a sybil farm's bets move in lockstep, unmasking their operator.
